episode_title: #308: Chris Gray – Does Your Business Need a Plan B?

real_qa.q: Why does Your Empire focus on buying one to two million dollar apartments in Sydney's eastern suburbs rather than larger properties?
real_qa.r: Properties in the one to two million dollar range in five to 15 kilometre radius suburbs like the eastern beaches have three story height limits and small blocks of 12, which means there is high demand, no more supply, and lots of buyers, sellers, and renters. Larger properties like ten to twenty million dollar houses have lower rental yields of one to two percent compared to three to four percent, making them harder to hold. The median price point of one to two million dollars also aligns with what the average person in these suburbs can afford to buy, rent, or sell.
real_qa.requete: Your Empire property investment strategy Sydney

real_qa.q: What is rent vesting and how does Chris Gray use it as a wealth building strategy?
real_qa.r: Rent vesting means renting emotionally where you want to live and investing where you get a higher return. Gray rents a property in a premium suburb while purchasing investment properties that generate higher rental yields. For example, he rents a six or seven million dollar apartment for two thousand dollars per week while owning one to two million dollar properties that generate three to four percent yields. This allows him to control a larger asset base while living in a more expensive property than he could afford to buy outright.
real_qa.requete: rent vesting strategy Australia wealth building

real_qa.q: How have the Australian government's recent negative gearing changes affected Your Empire's property investment strategy?
real_qa.r: The changes have not affected the strategy at all. Gray wrote in his book back in 2008 that investment returns should never be done for tax reasons because tax changes constantly, and wealth creation plans span 30, 40, or 50 years. Whether you save ten or fifteen thousand dollars per year in tax versus getting a fifty to one hundred thousand dollar discount on the purchase price makes minimal difference. The real value is capital appreciation, and if you never sell, you never pay the capital gains tax.
real_qa.requete: negative gearing changes Your Empire strategy Australia 2024

real_qa.q: What is the leverage advantage of property investment compared to shares or other investments?
real_qa.r: With one hundred thousand dollars in the bank, you might get five to ten percent return on shares or deposits, which equals five to ten thousand dollars per year. With property, you can leverage that same one hundred thousand dollars as a deposit to buy a five hundred thousand to one million dollar property. If the property appreciates five to ten percent, that generates a fifty to one hundred percent return on your actual capital invested, while banks will lend ninety to ninety-five percent on property because they know decent property will bounce back.
real_qa.requete: property investment leverage advantage over shares

real_qa.q: How can young Australians without parental property wealth enter the property market according to Your Empire?
real_qa.r: Gray gives the example of a young man earning fifty to sixty thousand dollars who partnered with his cousin from the military. Together they bought a seven hundred thousand dollar one-bedroom unit in Coogee as a fifty-fifty split. During COVID, when nothing was happening, it appreciated twenty to thirty percent and became worth nine hundred fifty thousand to one million dollars. A year or two later, he refinanced, pulled the equity out, refinanced while earning six figures, and bought a one-bedroom in Neutral Bay by himself.
real_qa.requete: young Australians enter property market without parental wealth

guest.bio_context: Chris Gray is one of the founding fathers of buyers agents in Australia and a pioneer in the property investment space. He is an accountant by training and has written books on wealth building strategy through property investment. He has been actively buying and managing properties in Sydney's eastern suburbs for over 25 years, with a focus on one to two million dollar apartment units in premium locations like Coogee, Bondi, and Manly.
